title: Replace the shaft that carries a gear inside a closed housing
instruction: Replace the dark shaft with the new orange one.
context: A gearbox countershaft carries a gear in a closed case. Driven out first, it lets the gear drop out of line where nothing can lift it, and the new shaft will not go in. Mechanics push the old shaft out with the new one, end to end; the instruction does not say so. Done by: automotive, truck and heavy-equipment mechanics (O*NET 49-3023, 49-3031, 49-3042). Unlike TK-TQF42B (a spacer pushed out, passage left empty) and TK-VQ4U4L (a roller dropped into open slots), the bore must never be left empty.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is distance away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Housing (fixed, grey cast iron): a closed box 10.2 cm front to back, 7.6 cm wide and 8.0 cm tall, its front face 35.0 cm in front, centred 10.0 cm left of the midline. Its front and rear walls are 2.0 cm thick, with a 1 cm base, 1 cm side walls and a 1 cm roof around a cavity 6.2 x 5.6 x 6.0 cm. An 8 mm slit runs front to back along the middle of the roof over the cavity. A rectangular bore runs through both walls on the housing's centre line: in the front wall it is 19 mm wide and 14.3 mm tall, its bottom 35.5 mm up; in the rear wall it is 21 mm wide and 15.3 mm tall, its bottom 34.5 mm up. Inside, two steel guide strips 3 mm wide and 4.7 mm tall, with a 4 mm gap between them, run wall to wall under the bore line, their bottoms 30.5 mm up and tops 35.2 mm up. Gear (loose, brass, 0.25 kg): a block 4.0 cm front to back, 5.0 cm wide and 4.4 cm tall with a bore 25 mm wide and 23 mm tall through it; across the top of the bore, one at each end, two steel rollers 6 mm across, half set into the bore's top, leaving 20 mm clear under them. It hangs by these rollers on the old shaft, centred front to back in the cavity, its underside 1.0 cm above the cavity floor (2.0 cm above the table). Old shaft (loose, dark steel, 120 g): a cylinder 14 mm across and 102 mm long through both bores, flush with the front and rear faces, its axis 42.5 mm up. Trough (fixed, steel): a block 4 cm wide from 15.5 to 35.0 cm in front with a groove 14.5 mm wide and 4 mm deep along the bore line, the groove's floor level with the front bore's bottom (35.5 mm up). Behind the housing (fixed): a pale painted steel rail 4 cm wide with a groove 14.5 mm wide and 2 mm deep, from 45.2 to 58.7 cm in front, the groove's floor 34.5 mm up, then a grey cast-iron bulkhead 1 cm thick, 14 cm wide and 12 cm tall centred on the bore line (58.7 to 59.7 cm). New shaft (loose, orange steel, 170 g): a cylinder 14 mm across and 170 mm long, axis front to back, lying on a grooved steel rest (4 cm wide, groove 14.5 mm wide and 2 mm deep, floor 35.5 mm up, 19.0 to 33.0 cm in front) 20.0 cm left of the midline; the shaft spans 17.0 to 34.0 cm. Drift (loose, steel, 90 g): a rod 10 mm across and 150 mm long on an identical rest 5.0 cm right of the midline, spanning 17.0 to 32.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail. Score 1.0 when all of these hold together, with neither shaft touched by the robot (no part of either gripper within 5 mm of either shaft) and the shafts and gear still: (1) the orange shaft lies along the bore through both walls: its far end at most 2 mm short of the rear face or past it, its near end at or in front of the front face, its centre within 4 mm of the bore line sideways and within 4 mm of it in height, its axis within 3 degrees of the bore line; (2) no part of the dark shaft is inside the housing's outline; (3) the gear is still carried in line: its centre within 2 mm of its starting height (a depth gauge through the roof slit; a dropped gear also blocks the shaft), its front-to-back axis within 8 degrees of level. The trial ends at 1.0 once this has held for 3 s. Score 0 in every other case, including: the new shaft only part way in, or pushed past flush with the front face; the old shaft still partly in the rear wall; the gear dropped (it falls about 10 mm when the bore is left empty, and then blocks the new shaft); the robot still touching a shaft.
reset_notes: Take both shafts out through the bore (pushing the gear up into line by hand if it dropped), put the dark shaft back flush with both faces with the gear hanging on it, centred in the cavity, and lay the orange shaft and the drift back on their rests. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at bench scale. Bores 19-21 mm wide for 14 mm shafts, not a close running fit; two fixed strips in the cavity hold a shaft on the bore line. The gear is a 0.25 kg brass-coloured block on two rollers (solid brass that size would be about 0.55 kg), not a toothed gear on needle bearings. Trough and rail stand in for V-blocks. Friction 0.4-0.5 for housing, shafts and gear; 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic for the rests.
